In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we propose a novel approach for transfer learning between classification tasks, which we call Aspect-augmented Adverarial Networks (AAN), that learns to encode documents by selecting sentences relevant to a particular aspect.
the proposed approach outperforms all baselines and model variations in all experiments and on two different datasets.
we introduce a neural method to transfer knowledge from a labeled source domain to an unlabeled target domain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our model learns to encode documents in a way that it is invariant to the aspect of the sentence, and thus can transfer the knowledge of the source aspect to the target aspect.
we have proposed a novel method to learn a shared representation for two different classification tasks, where each task has its own set of keywords.
we introduce the idea of using keywords as a proxy for document labels and show that this can lead to better performance in domain adaptation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
aspect-augmented adversarial networks (AAAN) are a promising direction for domain adaptation in text classification.

, for transfer learning, it may be more effective to train a classifier on encoded documents rather than labels, and that aspect-augmented adversarial training is an effective means to transfer knowledge between tasks or aspects.
